dev_environment: Development PC without the YuE2 install: stand-in runtime with FFmpeg 8.1.1 (Rubber Band), Python 3.11, numpy/scipy/soundfile/librosa and placeholder model files.
adjust_checks: Validation rejects out-of-range, fractional, boolean, string and unknown values for key, tempo, mode and reverb.
Measured pitch and length after +12 semitones, 50% tempo, -5 semitones at 125%, and Slowed 80%, with both Rubber Band and the asetrate/atempo fallback.
Reverb adds a decorrelated stereo tail after a dry burst and keeps the exact length.
Pipeline shifts source.wav before generation (stays PCM_16), YuE2 receives the new length, reverb is applied to the result before validation.
A/B jobs share the adjustment; analysis reuse is refused when the adjustment differs; slowing past 10 minutes is rejected without creating jobs.
Derived works: new job with its own name and group, WAV/MP3 export, original audio unchanged, download names, chained adjustments, rejected requests leave no jobs.
browser_verified: Global key/tempo panel: Slowed / Sped up locks the key slider to the speed, reverb toggle and amount, persisted to settings
Per-song override copies the shared setting, saves Key -2 / Tempo 90%, shown in the song summary
Queue confirmation shows the shared key/tempo row; queued A/B jobs carry the per-song override and new names
Live pipeline shifted the reference with Rubber Band: 30 s to 33.333 s, -2 semitones (generation itself unavailable on the development PC)
My Works dialog: name and length preview, derived Slowed 80% + Reverb 40 work completed in 4 s as 37.5 s WAV + MP3 under the original
No browser console errors; forest-green and ivory layout kept
pending: Run benchmark_adjust.py on the RTX 5070 PC with real YuE2 and --validation dual-version/VALIDATION-v1.3.0.json (sets passed)
Subjective listening of shifted, slowed and reverb results
validation_limitations: No real YuE2 inference was possible on the development PC; generation with a shifted reference still needs the benchmark on the app PC.
The installed app's FFmpeg may lack Rubber Band; the asetrate/atempo fallback is tested but sounds less clean on large shifts. benchmark_adjust.py records which method the app PC uses.
